item.title: ‘You should've stayed': Anderson QB Cove Darbyshire still healing from father's suicide
item.description: Anderson Trojans quarterback Cove Darbyshire (7) celebrates beating the Friendswood Mustangs 34-35 in a Class 5A Division I Bi-District Round playoff game at House Park, Nov. 15, 2025. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) C overt "Cove" Darbyshire always pictured his mom and dad walking the field with him on Senior night. Instead, the Anderson quarterback told the American-Statesman last week he felt a surge of emotions as he and his mother, Marion, took the stroll alone on the last Friday of October. A touch of understanding. Some sadness, and definitely anger. He turned to his mom. "He's not here," Marion recalled her son saying. "That f-r." Chad Darbyshire was found dead by suicide Sept. 5, 2021, two days after Cove's 13th birthday. He was 49 years old. His death rocked Cove, his mom, his older brother Blaise and his older sister Zuzu, who are processing their emotions to this day. But none of them were shocked. The Darbyshires knew Chad wasn't well. Marion learned he suffered from depression a year into their marriage. Despite her best efforts, he never quite opened up to her, or anyone, about the depth of his pain and where it stemmed from. Chad, a former creative director, artist and sketch writer, lit up rooms with his charisma, she said. He was the kind of person others loved to be around. To his family, he could be volatile, brilliant, complicated. Cove Darbyshire in his room at home in Austin, Nov. 10, 2026. Behind him, two of his father's drawings are displayed on the wall. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) The Darbyshires' story is imperfect. But as Cove enters the playoffs, he still wishes his father was in the stands, no matter how much he resents him for leaving. "It's ugly. It's hard. And no one should ever have to go through it," Marion said. "Because no matter how bad they might have been, you always wish they were here." 'Just play football' Cove Darbyshire said he didn't know he wanted to get serious about football until the seventh grade - the year his father died. He played a variety of sports until then, with soccer being the main alternative. Cove has had an athletic build from birth (Marion said he was born with a six-pack) but the family didn't know what he actually wanted to do with it. Then, the day after their dad's memorial, Blaise Darbyshire remembers Cove walking into his room around 10 p.m. He asked Blaise to wake him up at 5:30 a.m. so that he could go work out at Dell Jewish Community Center in Northwest Hills. The routine continued throughout Cove's entire seventh grade and half his eighth-grade year. He'd told his older siblings he wanted to make it to the NFL. Blaise, who took a year off college to grieve, was more than willing to help. "You've told me your goal," Blaise recounted to the Statesman in October. item.title: Man Utd sack manager Carrick, with Pochettino set for hot seat
item.description: Michael Carrick has paid the price for Manchester United's disastrous start to the season (Oli SCARFF) Manchester United sacked manager Michael Carrick on Thursday after their worst-ever start to a Premier League campaign, with USA boss Mauricio Pochettino widely tipped to replace him. Former United captain Carrick led the team to an impressive third-place finish last season, but they have taken just eight points from 10 games in the current campaign and are in the relegation zone. The club confirmed in a statement that it had parted ways with the 45-year-old, following mounting speculation he would be axed during the international break. "After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions," United's statement said. "Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club." United said they intended to appoint a permanent successor "as quickly as possible". - Chaos - Carrick impressed after taking over as interim boss following Ruben Amorim's acrimonious exit in January, leading United to Champions League qualification. He was rewarded with a two-year permanent deal but, hampered by the club's underwhelming recruitment in the summer transfer window, his side have endured a steep decline this season. Carrick has struggled to maintain discipline, dropping captain Bruno Fernandes after he criticised his manager's tactics following a 4-1 thrashing at Champions League debutants Como. And defender Lisandro Martinez spoke out against the club's hierarchy over their lack of top-quality signings. Carrick's final game in charge was a chaotic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday, after which he stressed he would not walk away. United, however, have decided to act in the hope of saving their season after a paltry three wins from 15 games in all competitions. It is believed Carrick's future was decided on Wednesday during a meeting in Monaco involving co-owner Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox. Ex-Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, most recently in charge of Germany, were in the early running but Pochettino has now emerged as the overwhelming favourite to be announced as Carrick's successor. The Argentine has extensive experience of the Premier League following spells in charge of Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and he also coached Paris Saint-Germain. Pochettino signed a contract extension to remain with the USA through to the 2030 World Cup just three months ago. But Sky Sports reported Wednesday that United have "reached a verbal agreement in principle" with Pochettino, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford on several previous occasions, to become their new boss. item.title: Will Joseph and Max Ojomoh given chance to shine in radical England revamp for Japan
item.description: Will Joseph and Max Ojomoh have been given opportunities to impress in a much-changed starting side for an injury-hit England against Japan . Joseph will start on the wing and earn his first cap since the 2022 tour of Australia, while Ojomoh returns at inside centre for the first time since a player-of-the-match performance against Argentina last November. Henry Pollock earns just a second international start at No 8 after an eye-catching outing on the wing from the bench in the 45-22 success against Australia. George Ford starts ahead of Fin Smith at fly half, with Freddie Steward at full-back, Cadan Murley on the left wing and Jack van Poortvliet and Henry Slade the only backline starters retained from the Wallabies win. George Ford starts at fly half for England (Getty) Among the replacements, scrum half Archie McParland is in line for a debut, while Emmanuel Iyogun, Arthur Clark and Greg Fisilau will win their second caps. Steve Borthwick ’s squad had been hit by injuries to Ollie Chessum (shoulder), Seb Atkinson (hip), George Furbank (groin) and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, with the hope that the former trio can feature against New Zealand next week. Feyi-Waboso has been ruled out of the remainder of the Nations Championship with an ankle issue. “Japan are a very well-coached side who will challenge us in different ways, and we know we’ll need to bring intensity throughout the game,” Borthwick said. “We’re all delighted for Archie. He’s had some bad luck with injury, so it’s especially pleasing to be able to name him in an England matchday 23 for the first time. He’s an outstanding young talent who has worked hard to get to this point, and we’re really looking forward to being back on Saturday.” Northampton’s Archie McParland will make his England debut (PA Wire) Fin Smith is understood to have trained fully this week but drops out of the matchday 23 entirely, perhaps with one eye on New Zealand next weekend. Marcus Smith again provides fly half cover as one of two backs on the bench. Alex Coles moves to the blindside with Chessum absent having scrummaged on the flank against Australia, and Asher Opoku-Fordjour is given a rare outing on the tighthead. In all, just five starters retain their spots, with Coles and Ben Earl among them but having moved positions. Japan, meanwhile, stick with a settled selection with Eddie Jones naming an unchanged forward pack from the defeat to Wales. Former England boss Eddie Jones takes his Japan side to Twickenham on Saturday (PA Wire) Riku Tokito is brought in on the wing for the injured Inoke Burua and will make his debut. The former Japan sevens international is yet to play a professional 15-a-side game, though Jones is confident he can handle an anticipated aerial bombardment from England. “It’s a big week for Japanese rugby,” Jones said. “England is the nation we’ve never been able to beat. item.title: Tom Brady vs. Will Smith: Which Celebrity’s Team Will Win the E1 Championship?
item.description: The electric-boat league will crown a new winner this weekend. The Bombay Sapphire E1 Miami Grand Prix, taking place on Biscayne Bay on November 13 and 14, will determine this season’s champions . Teams backed by A-listers including Tom Brady, Rafael Nadal, Will Smith, Marc Anthony, LeBron James, and Steve Aoki will compete in two races on consecutive days, marking the championship’s first double-header. More from Robb Report Mercedes-Benz's New Holographic Tech Will Turn Your Windshield Into a Screen Chris Hemsworth's New Gin Was Made Using Honey From His Australian Farm This $14 Million Equestrian Estate Sits Within a Double-Gated Orange County Community “This is set to be an incredible finale to the 2026 Championship and a landmark weekend for E1 as we stage our first double-header,” E1 C.E.O. Jamie Copas said in a statement. “ With two races on consecutive days, there is still much to play for as teams look to finish the season on a high.” Team Brady, which won the opening two E1 world titles in 2024 and 2025, respectively, looks particularly strong heading into the championship showdown. Pilots Emma Kimiläinen and Sam Coleman have been on the podium at every round this year, securing 157 points for the team. The E1 Jeddah GP in January. Photo by Malcolm Griffiths/Getty Images That’s not to say Team Brady has it in the bag. Will Smith’s Westbrook Racing is trailing 40 points behind, but could still clinch the championship. Pilots Sara Price and Lucas Ordóñez, who have notched 82 points throughout the season, will have to need to return to the winning form they had earlier in the races and sweep the weekend to become victors. As for who comes next, Steve Aoki’s Aoki Racing Team sit third with 86 points, while LeBron’s Team AlUla are just two points further back. A podium finish would be especially meaningful for Aoki, given the DJ was born in Miami. “Amazing to see my team tearing it up in my home race again,” adds Aoki. “We fought all season to get our way into the Championship top three, and there’s no better place to finish the season strong than in front of a Miami crowd.” Those in Miami can watch the E1 RaceBirds “fly” across the water from the E1 Ocean Club. Title partner Bombay Sapphire is also holding an exclusive race-day celebration on a private Team Brady yacht docked at the Ocean Club. (Passes for E1 Ocean Club are available through Fever .) item.title: Siena basketball's win at Dayton brings back great memories for Fenlon
item.description: Siena senior Conner Fenlon scores at the end of the second half of their 86-75 victory over Canisius at the Times Union Center on Sunday Feb. 26, 2012 in Albany, N.Y. He finished with a career high five points. (Philip Kamrass / Times Union ) (Philip Kamrass) After reenacting one of the great moments in Siena men's basketball history, Saints radio analyst and former player Conner Fenlon watched from the press table as the program added to its memorable history at University of Dayton Arena. He and play-by-play partner Emmanuel Berbari called Siena's 99-89 victory over the Flyers of the Atlantic 10 on Tuesday night before a sellout crowd of 13,407. It was a signature road win for the Saints in Nevada Smith's third game as head coach. "You're going on the road, early in the season, A10-level team," Fenlon said Wednesday. "The one thing about Dayton, they love their basketball there. They've sold out every year for I don't know how long (97 straight home games). They've got a good team. For Siena to go in there and play as well as they did, almost 100 points put on a team like that on the road, says a lot about Coach Smith and what these guys are believing in what he's preaching." It was Fenlon's first time in UD Arena since he was a Siena freshman walk-on guard in 2008-09. The ninth-seeded Saints knocked off No. 8 Ohio State 74-72 in double overtime in an NCAA Tournament first-round game. The victory is best remembered for point guard Ronald Moore's two 3-pointers. The first tied the game with 3.5 seconds left in the first overtime. The second won the game with 3.9 seconds left in the second overtime. Fenlon celebrated with his teammates on the Siena bench. "I haven't been there in a long time and it brought back a lot of memories," said Fenlon, 36, who is a controller at Albany Steel in Menands. "I always say, I don't think I'm in the position I am now if it wasn't for those teams and the success we had. It was so much fun to be back there." Siena also defeated Alcorn State in an NCAA opening-round game in Dayton in 2002, six years before Fenlon's arrival. After the team's morning shootaround on Tuesday, Siena assistant athletic director for communications Mike Demos wanted to recreate Moore's game-winner. With Berbari filming, Demos imitated former Siena guard Edwin Ubiles, who up-faked and passed the ball to Moore on the right wing for the winning shot. Except this time it was Fenlon, who still coaches AAU basketball but hadn't shot the ball in a big arena in a long time. "It was just for some fun and a laugh," said Fenlon, who posted the video on his X account @_cjf20. "The whole team was watching because they were putting their shoes on. Had a little pressure. I missed the first two, but ended up hitting the third." Once the real game started, Siena junior point guard Pace Prosser put on a performance against Dayton that would have made Moore proud. item.title: Donte Whitner names team that will stop the Minnesota Vikings from getting to the Super Bowl after Kirk Cousins trade
item.description: Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings have been solid defensively this season but their quarterback position had been a problem up until the Kirk Cousins trade. Carson Wentz once again struggled in the Vikings’ last game against the Buffalo Bills. He has one of the lowest completion rates (48.4%) in the NFL this season, which was causing problems for Minnesota on the offence. By contrast, Cousins has managed a 64.1% completion rate for the Las Vegas Raiders to this point and has 2,340 passing yards. But despite Cousins looking like a big upgrade for the Vikings, Donte Whitner still thinks they will struggle to get to the Super Bowl. Speaking via the NFL Network, Whitner suggested the arrival of Cousins could help them ‘all the way to the NFC Championship’ but the San Francisco 49ers could be the team that stops them reaching the Super Bowl. He said: “Minnesota’s defence, they have been carrying this team on their backs. “Kirk Cousins just showed up to help move the furniture. And if all goes well, like Kyle said, he could be moving that furniture all the way to the NFC Championship. “I’m not going to say Super Bowl yet because I still think they’re going to have to overcome the San Francisco 49ers.” Still, it will be interesting to see how the Vikings now look with a new quarterback when they clash with the Green Bay Packers this weekend. As for the 49ers, they, on paper, have a fairly easy game against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 10. item.title: Pep Guardiola to USMNT? Legendary manager emerges as SHOCK candidate to replace Mauricio Pochettino as Man Utd move nears
item.description: Manchester City v Chelsea FC - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Pep Guardiola has emerged as a spectacular candidate to take over the United States men's national team if Mauricio Pochettino leaves for Manchester United. The former Manchester City manager is currently a free agent and has previously expressed a deep admiration for the long-term sporting potential of the country. Shock candidate for USMNT United have officially dismissed Carrick , creating a major managerial domino effect. USMNT boss Pochettino has emerged as the overwhelming favourite to take the reins at Old Trafford . This sudden development has forced US Soccer to search for potential successors. According to The Athletic , Guardiola has been discussed at multiple levels within the USMNT hierarchy as a top candidate. The 55-year-old is currently without a club after his ten-year spell at Manchester City ended this summer . An ambitious American dream Appointing Guardiola would represent a monumental coup for American football, but the move remains highly speculative. The Spanish tactician has never managed at the international level and is accustomed to working with global superstars like Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland. However, Guardiola has previously expressed genuine admiration for the country. Speaking in 2024, he revealed his intrigue regarding American football. "The USA is fascinating when it comes to building a long-term project and taking the national team to the next level," Guardiola stated. "The potential of the USA is there given the population, the different sports and all of that." Guardiola also has a personal connection to the United States. Following his departure from Barcelona in 2012, he spent a year-long sabbatical living in New York. Overcoming the European competition Guardiola has already rejected international offers since leaving City. Earlier this year, he turned down the chance to manage the Italy national team to prioritise a personal sabbatical. Italian football federation president Giovanni Malago confirmed the approach to La Repubblica . Malago explained: "Pep was honest. He took some time out, also for family reasons. But if he had done something, he would have done it with us." Awaiting the Old Trafford domino Any formal approach from US Soccer depends entirely on Pochettino finalising a move to United. Until the Premier League club appoint Carrick's official successor, the USMNT managerial situation remains in limbo. If Pochettino does depart after this international break, the international schedule could work in Guardiola's favour. The USMNT do not play their next competitive fixtures until March, meaning the Spaniard could continue his planned break for several more months before returning to the dugout. For now, the football world will watch closely to see if United secure Pochettino. If they do, US Soccer could launch one of the most audacious managerial pursuits in history.

item.title: Mississippi State’s 41 points without Kamario Taylor explain his reported $7.5 million deal to return in 2027
item.description: Kamario Taylor is finalizing a deal to return to the Mississippi State Bulldogs in 2027 that will make him the highest-paid quarterback in college football, On3’s Chris Low and Pete Nakos reported Wednesday . The deal is worth $7.5 million and could climb past $9 million with incentives. Taylor has played less than a quarter of football since Oct. 3, and Mississippi State is paying him like a player who never left the field. With Taylor healthy, Mississippi State opened 4-0 and scored 172 points, an average of 43 per game, capped by a 31-24 win over the No. 19 Missouri Tigers on Sept. 26. He hurt his toe in that game, played through it in a 56-23 loss to the Alabama Crimson Tide, sat out at the LSU Tigers and left the Oklahoma Sooners game in the first quarter. The school announced on Oct. 27 that he would miss the rest of the season with a foot injury requiring surgery and said he is expected to return at 100 percent. Oct 24, 2026; Starkville, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi State Bulldogs quarterback Kamario Taylor (1) passes the ball during warm ups prior to the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images In the four games Taylor either missed or did not finish, Mississippi State scored 41 points total. The Bulldogs were shut out 31-0 at LSU, lost 23-15 to Oklahoma, managed three points in a 31-3 loss to the Texas Longhorns and dropped a 25-23 decision at home to the Vanderbilt Commodores last Saturday. A team that climbed to No. 16 in the AP poll at the end of September now sits at 4-5 on a five-game losing streak, and those 41 points are the clearest measure available of what Taylor is worth to it. Why Mississippi State moved on Kamario Taylor before the portal ESPN’s Pete Thamel posted Wednesday that the deal was expected to be completed later in the day and called it significant for head coach Jeff Lebby’s portal recruiting and roster building. He then passed along what a source told ESPN about the effect Taylor has on other players. “One of the thing we realized is the level of quality players who are intrigued by joining Kamario at Mississippi State,” the source said. Lebby heads into the transfer window with a five-game skid on the books, a 5-8 finish in 2025 and a team that needs two wins in its last three games just to reach .500. A signed quarterback is the one thing a portal target can see on a depth chart before he commits, and Taylor’s 4-0 start is the most recent picture of what this program looks like with a full-strength offense. item.description: MIAMI GARDENS ― The Miami Dolphins starting quarterback for at least the next four games had -142 rushing yards in four years of college football. So we're going to start out by suggesting this has nothing to do with young backup Kyle McCord , who demonstrated a good arm, attack mindset and confident leadership at Ohio State and Syracuse. (For the record, lost yardage by sacks count in quarterback rushing totals in college. McCord did have 240 total college rushing yards excluding sacks.) This is about Miami's long-term quarterback situation, which remains unclear. Malik Willis is a dynamic, explosive, exciting runner ― when healthy. Willis is also now sidelined following injuries to a toe, thumb, groin and core this season. Willis needs rest, at a minimum. He has not looked like himself in the last two games, after being among the league leaders in quarterback rushing yards earlier this season. "This is the best decision for him," Miami coach Jeff Hafley said. This is where we tell you that whether it's Malik Willis or some other unknown quarterback, the best long-term decision for Miami at quarterback is to have a quarterback who can run. Most of the best teams have quarterbacks who can extend plays, escape danger, bail teammates out and earn first downs and more, on the run. And if there is a slightly higher injury risk for those quarterbacks, so be it. The upside is worth the risk. I asked Hafley how he weighs and balances the fact that mobile, athletic quarterbacks create an enormous benefit on game day, but might also face an increased risk of injury. Hafley, a defensive play-caller and long-time defensive coordinator and defensive coach, knows how much more difficult it is to game plan for and handle a mobile quarterback on game day. As for injury risk? "Some that I've been around that go through a whole season playing that way and nothing happens," Hafley said. "And some guys, they get hit and something does happen. But then you get a guy who stays in the pocket and can't get out of the way and he's getting hit even more. So I mean, I think there's a balance between a pocket quarterback and a guy who has the ability to make plays. You're going to get hit regardless." He's right. Running quarterback. item.description: Liverpool forward could be set for January move despite recent performances Liverpool weigh January loan for Will Wright amid academy development push Liverpool head into the international break in decent shape, fourth in the Premier League after 10 matches, and that matters. Early work under Andoni Iraola has been solid, organised and largely sensible. Still, league position can hide a few things. This squad needs refining, and the next transfer window looks less like a luxury and more like routine maintenance. According to the Daily Mail, one of the more interesting January calls concerns not a glamorous signing, but a possible loan for academy striker Will Wright. That tells you something about where Liverpool are. Recruitment is not only about buying, it is about sequencing development properly and avoiding stagnation for younger players. Wright, 19, has built a strong case for senior football. He has 13 goals in all competitions, boosted by a hat-trick in the 5-3 win over Fenerbahce, and he has already picked up an England youth call-up. There is no mystery here. Liverpool think regular men’s football could speed up his progress, and there should be plenty of interest if they decide to send him out. That decision, sensibly, will involve Iraola. This is important because Liverpool’s current head coach has shown a willingness to use younger players. Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas and Luke Chambers have all had chances, and that matters more than broad slogans about pathways. A pathway only counts when minutes are actually available. Iraola is said to be in regular contact with academy staff, including Rob Page, Alex Inglethorpe and Luiz Fernando Iubel. That should be standard at a serious club, but it often is not. The detail about Iubel, Julian Ward and loans manager Gary Probert watching Wright’s hat-trick in Turkey suggests Liverpool are trying to make this call on evidence rather than hype. Wright’s story is straightforward. He joined from Salford City in August 2025 after making his senior debut there during the 2024/25 season. He had already featured in the EFL Trophy, FA Cup and League Two, then stepped into Liverpool’s Under 21s, scored six goals in his first campaign and later made a pre-season senior appearance against Athletic Club at Anfield. He was also named in a Premier League matchday squad in April 2026. Progress has been steady. Andoni Iraola faces practical January choices The question for Liverpool is timing. item.title: 21 sixes in an innings! New Zealand batter Bevon Jacobs comes close to world record
item.description: New Zealand batter Bevon Jacobs produced a stunning batting display in the domestic Ford Trophy on Thursday, smashing an unbeaten 202 off just 137 balls against Otago in Auckland. The 21 sixes in his innings set a new record for the most sixes hit by a New Zealand batter in a List A innings. Jacobs was just two sixes short of the world record of 23, held by Australia's Da’Arcy Short. His powerful knock helped Auckland post 334/8 at the Kennards Hire Community Oval. However, Jacobs' effort went in vain as Otago chased down the target in 49.1 overs. A total of 34 sixes were hit in the match. Jacobs hits 21 sixes in record-breaking knock Batting at No. 4, Jacobs turned his maiden List A century into a double century with some powerful hitting. He reached the 200-run mark in just 137 balls, hitting seven fours and 21 sixes. The 21 sixes are the most by a New Zealand batter in a List A innings. Jacobs came close to breaking the world record, which belongs to Australia's Da’Arcy Short. Short had hit 23 sixes while scoring 257 off 148 balls for Western Australia against Queensland in Sydney in 2018. — MargotButcher (@MargotButcher) Jacobs also became only the fourth New Zealand batter to score a double century in List A cricket. He joined Jamie How (2012), Martin Guptill (2015) and Chad Bowes (2024) on the list. His 202 not out was also a record score for Auckland Aces in the Ford Trophy and the third double century in the tournament's history. — thenichecache (@thenichecache) From India series to domestic record Jacobs recently featured in New Zealand's five-match T20I series against India. item.title: Mike Brown points out what was ‘very alarming’ about Jalen Brunson during Knicks’ loss to Cavaliers
item.description: Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images Mike Brown noticed something about Jalen Brunson’s performance against the Cleveland Cavaliers that truly shocked him. After a strong string of recent results, the Knicks were beaten by the Cavaliers at home in a result that left many of their fans very disappointed. Despite their talent, the Cavaliers aren’t considered a strong team this season, so a loss to them isn’t a good look for the reigning world champions. Mike Brown believes Jalen Brunson deserves a ‘better whistle’ after 0-FT game Speaking after the New York Knicks’ loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers, head coach Mike Brown discussed their performance and what caused their loss. In particular, he pointed to their free-throw disparity and pointed out how a player like Jalen Brunson getting zero free-throw attempts was quite concerning. Mike Brown said: “It’s a possession game, and we lost it in the category. They had 14 more free-throw attempts than us, four more offensive rebounds, and two less turnovers. When that happens against a good team, it’s going to be hard to win the game. So, I give them a lot of credit. “I am a little surprised Jalen [Brunson] played almost 35 minutes, and he had zero free-throw attempts. That’s pretty alarming. I’m not sure how or why it was that way. I know at one time, the free-throw advantage was 18-3. “That’s not why we lost the game, but you hope you get a better whistle when you’re playing a good team like that because it’s already hard enough to go win a game. That was part of the reason why we lost the possession game.” Brunson did have a decent scoring performance, delivering 27 points, while shooting 12/27 from the field and 3/8 from beyond the arc. However, him not getting to the free-throw line does come as a surprise, as the last time he had a game with zero free-throw attempts was back in February of this year against the Philadelphia 76ers. For a player of Brunson’s offensive prowess, seeing him fail to draw a single foul in the shooting process during a game is quite startling. item.title: Lindblad and Lawson to continue at Racing Bulls
item.description: Arvid Lindblad (left) and Liam Lawson have taken Racing Bulls to fifth place in the constructors' championship on 114 points, 45 points ahead of Alpine [Getty Images] Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson will continue as the drivers for Red Bull's second team Racing Bulls in 2027. Red Bull had been deciding whether to promote Bulgarian Formula 2 front-runner Nikola Tsolov in place of Lawson but have decided to spend a second season assessing their current line-up. Team principal Alan Permane said: "I have no doubt that this is the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition. "Both have demonstrated their ability and potential throughout the season, and we've seen the progress they've made, both individually and as a pairing." The decision to retain both marks a break from the previous Red Bull philosophy of fast-tracking drivers through the programme. Racing Bulls essentially exists to find potential drivers for the main Red Bull team, so the company has tended to jettison drivers who have been given a chance and not succeeded. That's why Lawson, 24, was considered vulnerable. He was promoted to Red Bull alongside Max Verstappen for the 2025 season only to be demoted after just two races in which he had struggled. The New Zealander has since sought to rebuild his career and was much more convincing when he was re-promoted to Red Bull for the Dutch, Italian and Spanish Grands Prix this year while regular driver Isack Hadjar was recovering from a broken wrist. Keeping Lawson on board for 2027 gives Red Bull a known-quality benchmark with which to continue their assessment of Lindblad, who made his debut this season. The 19-year-old Briton has excelled at times in his rookie year but on average has been a little behind Lawson, who has out-qualified him 13 times to nine and has scored more than twice as many points. Lawson said: "We've had a brilliant season together and the team has worked very hard to produce a fast car, which I've loved driving. "It feels great to be part of a historic season for the team as we continue our fight for fifth place in the constructors' championship. "I'm looking forward to carrying this moment forward with Arvid through to 2027; we're building something super positive and I'm excited by what we can achieve together." Lindblad added: "It's been a truly special year, full of new experiences and learnings since the very first pre-season test. I'd like to thank everyone for their trust and support. "I can't wait to get started next year, building on everything I've learned during my rookie season." The news release announcing the pairing made no mention of Tsolov, who is expected to be retained by Red Bull in some form of reserve role in which he gains experience through work in the simulator and with testing previous cars. item.description: Motorsport photo A Williams FW16 driven by three-time Formula 1 champion Ayrton Senna in his final season in the series is going under the hammer in New York. RM Sotheby's is offering chassis FW16B-01 in Sotheby's 'The Now & Contemporary Evening Auction', with an estimate of $4million to $6million (£2.95million to £4.45million). It is the first time the car has been put up for public sale. When the Brazilian driver joined Williams from McLaren in 1994, the Grove outfit agreed that he would receive one of its chassis if it won that year's constructors' championship. Senna tragically died at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix, in chassis FW16-02. Williams went on to beat Benetton to the constructors' crown, while Damon Hill lost the drivers' title to Michael Schumacher by a single point. At the end of the year, the team kept its word and gave FW16B-01 to Senna's family. According to RM Sotheby's, it is one of only two surviving FW16s that Senna drove, although he never raced the chassis himself. item.title: Smith's Netherlands switch sad - SA swimming boss
item.description: Tatjana Smith won one gold and one silver medal at both the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Olympic Games [Getty Images] The decision by South Africa's most decorated Olympian Tatjana Smith to switch allegiance to the Netherlands is "sad" for the nation, says Swimming South Africa CEO Zikie Molusi. Double Olympic champion Smith, who has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch, was in tears when she announced her decision on Wednesday. She said that the opportunity "offers greater high-performance support" and that South African athletes "deserve a system that gives them an opportunity to thrive, not just survive". "When I received that correspondence from Tatjana we understood because she has been really generous and kind enough to articulate the rationale that informed the decision," Molusi, the acting CEO of the governing body, told eNews Channel Africa: "A very sad decision for the country, particularly as we were preparing to take the team to Beijing for the short course World Championships in December." Tearful Smith switches allegiance to Netherlands Smith, formerly Schoenmaker, previously said financial worries, which included a dispute with Swimming South Africa over prize money, contributed to her decision to step away from the sport after the Paris 2024 Olympics. The 29-year-old, who has won four Olympic medals, came out of retirement in September and is set to represent the Netherlands for the first time at the World Championships from 1-6 December. Smith said representing the Netherlands would give her "the potential to build a more sustainable career". She said the "financial and practical challenges of swimming were among the reasons my previous career became difficult to sustain". Speaking to Radio 702, Molusi accepted that Swimming South Africa should not have withheld prize money from Smith following the 2023 World Championships. Molusi said that was caused by conflicting sponsorship agreements but it "shouldn't have happened". Of the 21 athletes competing for South Africa at the Worlds next month, Molusi said "probably 50% will be subsidised fully", with the rest receiving partial support. "It's an ecosystem issue within South African sport that possibly needs to be dealt with," Molusi said. "This comes as a result of the inadequate funding that sport federations are receiving."
